document.title: Afghanistan: Taliban Shift Yar Mohammad from Herat to Ghazni (Islama 00025)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban Biography: The Structure and Leadership of the Taliban 1996-2002
document.note: [Confidential] Mullah Omar moves Mullah Yar Mohammed from the governorship of Herat to Ghazni. The cable questions Omar's motives, including suppressing Yar Mohammad's independent power base, and whether he would accept the move. Excised.

events.description: Herat falls to the Taliban; Yar Mohammad becomes governor
Wahab confirms Mullah Omar shifted Yar Mohammad to Ghazni governor and appointed Abdul Razaq governor of Herat
A Taliban supporter tells US poloff the move may curb Mohammad's power base
Herat fell to the Taliban; Yar Mohammad became governor.
Afghan Embassy First Secretary Wahab told US poloff that Omar shifted Yar Mohammad to Ghazni.
Dr. Taleb told poloff Yar Mohammad moved because of experience with minorities.
Taliban supporter told poloff the move may be to prevent an independent power base in Herat.
Mullah Omar appointed Yar Mohammad governor of Ghazni and Abdul Razaq governor of Herat.

key_claims: Mullah Omar shifted Yar Mohammad from Herat governorship to Ghazni in early January 1997.
A Taliban supporter suggested the move aimed to prevent Yar Mohammad building an independent power base in Herat.
Yar Mohammad may refuse the order, as earlier attempts to move him failed.
Observers suggest he was sent to Ghazni because of his experience managing minorities amid Pashtun-Hazara tensions.
Abdul Razaq, known for military prowess, was named Herat governor.
Taliban and Akbari attacks on Khalili forces appear uncoordinated.
